summary: New supervision_budget module: hard-capped turn digests, escalate-token gating, primary-side tool allowlist enforcement, and per-turn token drift tracking
rationale: The supervisor/delegate model already budgets delegate tokens (delegate_token_budget) and context-fold allocations (fold_budget), but the primary agent's own context consumption during a supervised delegate run is ungoverned: turn digests can exceed the context window, tool-use escalation has no explicit cost, and there is no mechanism to block primary-side tools (read_file, bash, grep) when the supervisor has not paid for them. A dedicated supervision_budget module closes these gaps so the primary's context stays within bounds, every escalate call is attributed, and tool access is gated on a spent token.
acceptance_criteria: New files src/supervision_budget.c and src/headers/supervision_budget.h exist and compile; the module links into the aimee client/server binaries via the Makefile and CMakeLists.txt

Turn digest rendering calls supervision_budget_digest_cap() which clamps output to ≤16000 tokens per primary context window (re-using AGENT_CONTEXT_BUDGET from agent_types.h as the ceiling); verified by unit test with a synthetic 20k-token digest

supervision_budget_escalate_spend() decrements a per-session escalate-token counter, returns the remaining balance, and writes an audit_action_log row with caller attribution and args_hash (p2 dependency); unit test asserts log row and balance after N escalate calls

pre_tool_check (guardrails_orchestrator.c) consults supervision_budget_tool_allowed(): primary-side tools read_file, bash, and grep are blocked (pre_tool_check returns non-zero) when the escalate-token balance is zero; unit test asserts BLOCKED for each tool without an active token and PERMITTED after escalate_spend

supervision_budget_turn_record() appends (turn_index, prompt_tokens) to an in-memory primary_tokens_by_turn array; supervision_budget_drift_report() serialises the array as JSON for the infra tokens command; unit test asserts monotonic turn indices and correct JSON shape
Delegate economics (delegate_economics.c) calls supervision_budget_turn_record after each completed turn so the token curve stays populated during multi-turn delegate runs
All new unit tests pass under both make test and cmake --build + ctest
